subject: AB07CB83562E4E8FB296FD5FA74B7DB3
introduction: “We must pray for each other.” Most of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayers are not for himself. A letter arrives, and its answer ends with a prayer for the writer, for her family, for the friends of a town: that they be confirmed, illumined, made firm, made a cause of guidance. This guide gathers a hundred such intercessions. Paul’s letters open the same way, “making mention of you in my prayers”; Jesus prayed for Peter by name; the priestly blessing of Numbers is intercession made into liturgy; and the book of Job ends with a man restored “when he prayed for his friends”.
questions: What do these prayers most often ask for other people? What do they not ask?
How is praying for someone’s spiritual progress different from wishing they would change?
Whom would you find it hard to pray for in this way?

outside.why: Assist these friends to win Thy good pleasure. Paul for his friends: this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment.
Thou hearest my cry and my lamentation. The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
Give thanks for having attained unto this friend. Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
We must pray for each other. Pray one for another, that ye may be healed.
I offer prayers at the threshold for you. I cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers.
Make this assemblage radiant, the hearts merciful. The Lord bless thee, and keep thee: the Lord make his face shine upon thee.
Those present here, turning unto Thee. Where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
That which will bring joy to your eyes. Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
Servants who serve Thy Threshold. Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love.
I beseech the Manifest Beauty for you. I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
The Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. What does praying for another’s growth do to the one who prays?

shortfall: The hundred prayers ask blessing and progress for particular friends and gatherings in similar terms; companions were set to the first stretch only.
